# Allowed permissions for EVSwipe.
# Any uses-permission in a manifest NOT listed here FAILS the CI.
# Why: this app holds an accessibility service and draws over other apps — the classic
# Android malware pairing. Every new permission widens that surface and must be reviewed
# here, with the justification written down.
#
# One line = one full permission name. '#' = comment.

# --- Overlay ---
# The invisible swipe strips at the bottom edge and the floating back button are drawn
# over whatever app is in the foreground. Without this the app has no input surface at all.
android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW

# --- Own service ---
# A foreground service owns the overlay for as long as the head unit is on, and starts at
# boot so the swipe areas exist without the settings screen being opened first.
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE
# Since API 34 a foreground service must declare a type backed by a permission. The overlay
# service is none of the catalogued kinds — it draws the swipe strips and nothing else — so it
# runs as "special use". The type grants no capability of its own; it is what makes a
# foreground service legal at all on Android 14.
android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE
# Posts the service notification, which is the only visible sign the overlay is running.
android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED

# --- Network / OTA — UNSTABLE flavor only ---
# Declared solely in src/unstable/AndroidManifest.xml. The unstable channel self-updates
# (checks GitHub pre-releases, https + host allowlist + signature check). The stable APK
# has neither this permission nor any updater code: it is a fully offline app.
android.permission.INTERNET

# --- Note on the accessibility service ---
# BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE is not a uses-permission — it is the permission the AccService
# component *requires of the system*, which is how an accessibility service is declared.
# The capability it grants is bounded in res/xml/accessibility_service_config.xml:
# typeWindowStateChanged only, canRetrieveWindowContent="false". Widening either of those
# is a security change and belongs in a review, not in a drive-by commit.
